title: A probe that cannot run on this box is written as a fact about the blob
body:
## Summary
probeMissing records ffprobe's own failure as decodable:false; with ffprobe absent (ENOENT) or killed at its 30 s bound, every blob sinks as undecodable and is never re-probed.

## Description
packages/producers/src/media-facts/run.ts:154-170 passes any ProbeRead {ok:false} to factsOf, which writes undecodable with the error (core.ts:57). lib/producers/media-facts.ts:25-34 resolves ENOENT and a timeout kill to the same {ok:false,error}. The facts row then exists, so factsMissing never returns that blob again: a box missing ffprobe (or a LOCAL_BINARIES=off posture) turns the whole Library 'unreadable' permanently. Fix: the port distinguishes 'the tool did not run' (ProbeRead gains unavailable: true, set by the binding on ENOENT/timeout); run.ts puts those in `failed`, not in a fact.

## Flow
- ffprobe absent -> probe answers 'spawn ffprobe ENOENT'
- factsOf -> decodable:false row per blob
- next sync: factsMissing empty, items stay sunk
- fix: binding flags unavailable; run.ts counts it failed, writes nothing

## Expected impact
Operator on a fresh box sees every Library item flagged unreadable after one sync. Could break: a genuinely corrupt file that makes ffprobe hang would be retried each sync (bounded by the job's limit).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a box's missing tool is not a blob's fact
Before: walked: 4 blobs, probe ENOENT -> 4 undecodable rows, 0 missing next sync
After: predicted: 0 rows, 4 failed, 4 missing next sync
Method: simulation - the fix needs lib/producers/media-facts.ts (bound-producers) to set the flag; instrument is a fake MediaProbe answering ENOENT in tests/next-server/library-media-facts.test.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: probeMissing over a MediaProbe whose probe answers {ok:false,error:'spawn ffprobe ENOENT', unavailable:true}: count facts written and factsMissing after

title: A live upload whose record lost its claim keeps the platform id only in a dropped outcome
body:
## Summary
send() returns 'lost' with the YouTube id in its error, but nothing durable carries it; the worker timer keeps only a count.

## Description
packages/producers/src/publish/publish.ts:348-353: recordPublication fenced-refused after a live upload returns {kind:'lost', error:'... youtube holds it as <id>'}. lib/producers/publish.ts:190-203 publishTimers keeps n('lost') only. The slot shows the sweep's 'interrupted', no publication row exists, so priorPublicationIn does not block a re-schedule -> a second live upload of the same export. Fix: append an unfenced event (e.g. `publish.orphan`, subject the slot, data channel+platformId) when a live delivery cannot be recorded; Board/Calendar can then name it.

## Flow
- live upload completes, claim lost before record
- outcome 'lost' -> worker counts it
- operator reschedules the 'interrupted' slot -> second upload

## Expected impact
Prevents a duplicate upload on YouTube; adds one audit row (policy-tighten).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a delivered video is always findable from the store
Before: 0 durable records of a lost-after-delivery platform id
After: 1 event per such delivery
Method: simulation - needs a new event type in the kernel/domain (out of this round's paths) and a lost-claim-after-upload case
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: publish.test.ts: upload stub that steals the claim (sweep as OTHER) after returning ok; assert an event naming platformId exists

title: A captions failure after a live upload fails the slot without the video's id
body:
## Summary
The YouTube adapter inserts captions after uploadVideo inside one try; a captions error returns unavailable and the created video's id is lost.

## Description
lib/producers/publish.ts:97-107: `up` exists on YouTube when insertCaptions throws; the catch returns err('unavailable') and publish.ts:331 fails the slot with only the captions sentence. No publication, session not forgotten. Fix: on a post-upload failure return ok with the platform id and a `kept`-style note, or err carrying platformId so publish.ts records the publication and names the captions failure.

## Flow
- live upload succeeds
- captions insert 403
- slot failed 'captions...' ; retry may upload again

## Expected impact
A duplicate private video per captions failure avoided.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a delivered video is always recorded
Before: walked: 1 delivered video, 0 publications recorded
After: 1 publication with the captions failure named
Method: simulation - site is lib/producers/publish.ts (bound-producers), out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tests/next-server/publish-youtube.test.ts with a fetch stub that 403s the captions call: count publications
drain_note: needs a field on Delivered/UploadHooks in adapter.ts

title: The standing counts a slot's own pre-flight refusals as the channel failing
body:
## Summary
A snippet refusal, an export gone, or 'already published' lands as slot.fail and raises the channel's failuresSinceSuccess, though no request reached the platform.

## Description
packages/producers/src/publish/standing.ts:55-62 marks only interrupted/stopped as notTheChannel. packages/ui/src/components/floor/slot.ts breakOf (1d0328a6) already classifies nine pre-flight sentences as 'never sent'. The readiness row then shows 'last failure: title over 100 characters, 3 in a row' as the channel's health. Excluding them shows FEWER failures on the channel row (they stay on the slot) - a change to what the owner is told, so it waits for a ruling.

## Flow
- slot with '<' in title fails at plan
- standing: failuresSinceSuccess 1, lastError the snippet sentence
- readiness row reads it as YouTube failing

## Expected impact
Readiness row would stop blaming the channel for content errors; could hide a real pattern if the classification over-matches.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - channel health counts only what reached the channel
Before: 9 pre-flight sentences counted as channel failures
After: 0, if ruled
Method: simulation - policy question (logs less on the owner-facing row); instrument exists (slot.ts sentence list)
Result: better
Gate: policy-loosen

title: Every 30 s tick decodes every future slot to read the next one's time
body:
## Summary
publishTick's `next` calls listSlotsIn(scheduled, from now) and takes [0]; all future rows are zod-decoded each tick.

## Description
packages/producers/src/publish/tick.ts:157 reads the whole future schedule (ORDER BY at, id, readSlotRow per row) to use one `at`. A `limit` on @gt/kernel/slots/read listSlotsIn (or a min(at) read) is the fix; kernel is outside this round.

## Flow
- N scheduled future slots
- each tick: N row decodes for 1 value

## Expected impact
Small: N is dozens today; grows with a long calendar.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - rows decoded per tick
Before: N rows per tick
After: 1
Method: simulation - site needs a kernel read option (packages/kernel/src/slots/read.ts), out of scope
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: count readSlotRow calls in one publishTick over 50 future slots

title: A follow-up answer may still contradict itself on one fact (kills and confirms)
body:
## Summary
After the set check, two different kinds on one id (kills + downgrades, confirms + kills) still pass the door.

## Description
packages/producers/src/research/followUp.ts set check refuses repeats of a create or a relative op only. A kill beside a downgrade of the same fact applies in order (lib/research/revisions.ts) and the later lands 'no such id here'. Whether a contradictory answer is refused or reported is a product rule.

## Flow
- answer: kills f1, downgrades f1
- revisions: kill lands, downgrade 'no such id here'

## Expected impact
A reviewer sees a half-landed answer; refusing it costs a turn.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one answer, one coherent change
Before: accepted
After: refused, if ruled
Method: simulation - rule choice (refuse vs report) is the owner's
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
